results.title: Guard drops the attribute where it exists
results.reason: Every template wraps the attribute in #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, omitting it for net4x/netstandard2.0 consumers though the attribute exists there. Unity aside unverified.

results.title: README states a false availability limit
results.reason: README claims the attribute is unavailable on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework; reference assemblies define it on both with class targets.

results.title: Guard test only restates the template text
results.reason: Test counts textual guard+attribute occurrences and asserts equality; it never compiles output for netstandard2.0 or net4x, so proves nothing about availability.

results.title: Generator diagnostics and compile errors ignored
results.reason: Output compilation and diagnostics discarded via out _, out _; run result diagnostics never inspected; tests only check generated text.

results.title: Attribute on partial resolver hides user code
results.reason: Attribute is placed on the user-declared partial resolver class; C# merges attributes across partial declarations, so user-written members there are also excluded.
